title: BMW iX3 M60 xDrive Is an Electric SUV That Thinks It’s a Hot Hatch
summary: BMW has confirmed that the X3 M will not return, but that doesn’t mean buyers who want more performance from an SUV need to look elsewhere. The new BMW iX3 M60 xDrive partially fills the gap left by the X3 M as the quickest and most powerful iX3 variant. Like the iX M60, among other […]
body_markdown:
BMW has confirmed that the X3 M will not return, but that doesn’t mean buyers who want more performance from an SUV need to look elsewhere. The new BMW iX3 M60 xDrive partially fills the gap left by the X3 M as the quickest and most powerful[iX3](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/bmws-ambitious-ix3-packs-an-unusual-all-electric-driveline/) variant.


Like the iX M60, among other BMWs, the iX3 M60 xDrive is not a full-blown M model; It’s lumped under the M Performance label. M cars offer track-ready performance, while M Performance models balance performance with comfort and usability. This distinction sets the tone for the M60 xDrive: It’s quick, and it sounds like it’s fun to drive, but it’s not a direct replacement for the old X3 M.


Power comes from two motors (one per axle) that draw electricity from a 112.2-kilowatt-hour lithium-ion battery pack to develop 603 horsepower and 645 pound-feet of torque. That’s enough for a hot hatch-beating zero-to-60-mph time of 3.9 seconds and a 149-mph top speed. The list of standard features includes an Adaptive M suspension, variable sport steering, and an M Sport rear differential. BMW also added more bracing to the front end to increase transverse and torsional stiffness. If you get tired of driving, the optional Highway Assistant allows hands-free driving at up to 85 mph, though you still have to pay attention to the road ahead.

Several styling cues set the M60 apart from the standard iX3, and the overall design hints at the performance that’s packed into the drivetrain without veering into over-the-top territory. It features a deeper front bumper, trim-specific lighting elements across the front end, more aerodynamic door mirror caps, a diffuser integrated into the rear bumper, as well as new-look 21-inch wheels. The racing-inspired M Yellow Lights that first appeared on[the 2026 M Concept Neue Klasse](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/bmw-m-concept-neue-klasse-pictures/) are optional along with 22-inch wheels.


The M60’s interior layout mirrors the iX3’s, with a 17.9-inch touchscreen and the Panoramic Vision instrument cluster, but BMW added a more conventional-looking M Sport steering wheel that ditches the vertical spokes. M Sport 10-way power-adjustable front seats with a massage function are optional, which underlines that the M60 is more of a daily driver than a track beast.


Built in Hungary, the new BMW iX3 M60 xDrive will go on sale in January 2027. Pricing hasn’t yet been announced.
